claims.claim: Three pulses of 70 Gy within 1 day is a lethal dose killing the proliferating cells, including neoblasts, within 12 hr after irradiation.
claims.source: Taken together, the data shows that three pulses of 70 Gy within 1 day is a lethal dose killing the proliferating cells, including neoblasts, within 12 hr after irradiation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the irradiation experiments.

claims.claim: A multistep gating strategy based on a live cell Hoechst staining was developed to sort a population of differentiated cells with a 2C DNA content, and a population of proliferating cells in late S, G2, and M-phases with a 4C DNA content.
claims.source: A multistep gating strategy based on a live cell Hoechst staining was developed to sort a population of differentiated cells with a 2C DNA content, and a population of proliferating cells in late S, G2, and M-phases with a 4C DNA content (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
claims.evidence: This is stated as the FACS method and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Irradiation of animals before sorting resulted in a six-fold decrease of the fraction of cells in the 4C gate.
claims.source: Irradiation of animals before sorting resulted in a six-fold decrease of the fraction of cells in the 4C gate (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B), confirming that this gate represents proliferating cells and not contamination of e.g. doublets of differentiated cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a validation result and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: By comparing gene expression of the 2C and 4C cell populations of intact adult worms, 7124 transcript clusters were identified as significantly enriched in proliferating cells (S/G2/M cells), of which 5264 were upregulated by more than twofold.
claims.source: By comparing gene expression of the 2C and 4C cell populations of intact adult worms, we established a list of 7124 transcript clusters significantly enriched in proliferating cells (S/G2/M cells), of which 5264 were upregulated by more than twofold (Figure 3A and Figure 1—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from differential expression analysis and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The enriched GO terms in the list of genes enriched in S/G2/M cells include nucleic acid metabolic process, RNA processing, DNA replication, chromosome organization, and cell cycle processes.
claims.source: Similar to the irradiation experiments, the enriched GO terms in this list of genes include nucleic acid metabolic process, RNA processing, DNA replication, chromosome organization, and cell cycle processes (Figure 1—source data 3).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from GO term analysis.

claims.claim: The Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is the only significantly enriched type in S/G2/M cells (2.68-fold enrichment, p<10−15).
claims.source: Moreover, the Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is again the only significantly enriched type in S/G2/M cells (2.68-fold enrichment, p<10−15), whereas other tissue markers are enriched among transcripts specific for the G1 cell population (Figure 3A and Figure 1—source data 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from cell type enrichment analysis with statistical test.

claims.claim: 2739 transcript clusters enriched in the germline were identified.
claims.source: For this purpose, genes expressed in late-S/G2/M cells of intact worms (Figure 3A) were compared to genes expressed in late-S/G2/M cells of hatchlings (Figure 3B) and amputated heads (Figure 3C). Since the latter two conditions do not contain gonads, this allows distinguishing proliferating cells of germline and soma, and 2739 transcript clusters enriched in the germline were identified (Figure 3D and Figure 1—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The list of germline-enriched genes includes known germline-specific genes, such as macboule and melav.
claims.source: The list includes known germline-specific genes, such as macboule, melav (Sekii et al., 2009; Kuales et al., 2011), and several genes identified in the positional RNA-Seq dataset of M. lignano (Arbore et al., 2015) as gonad-specific (e.g. RNA815_7008, RNA815_9973.1, RNA815_1618.1, RNA815_2640, RNA815_7725.2, RNA815_12337.1).
claims.evidence: This is stated as validation of the germline gene list with citations.

claims.claim: Investigation of expression patterns of 27 candidate genes by in situ hybridization confirmed in all cases their expression in gonads, either in testes or in both testes and ovaries.
claims.source: Investigation of expression patterns of 27 candidate genes by in situ hybridization confirmed in all cases their expression in gonads, either in testes or in both testes and ovaries (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3–figure supplement 2 and Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a validation result and shown in the figures.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Mlig-cpeb1 resulted in enlarged testes, less distinct ovaries, and absence of developing eggs.
claims.source: In case of Mlig-cpeb1, the testes were enlarged, ovaries often became less distinct, and developing eggs were absent.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an RNAi phenotype observation.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx6 resulted in disappearance of both testes and ovaries, and worms obtained a wrinkled appearance.
claims.source: In case of Mlig-ddx6, both testes and ovaries disappeared, and worms obtained a wrinkled appearance.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an RNAi phenotype observation.

claims.claim: When tails were amputated at the eighth day of Mlig-ddx6 treatment, no blastema was formed, resulting in the lack of regeneration.
claims.source: When tails were amputated at the eighth day of treatment, no blastema was formed, resulting in the lack of regeneration (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as an RNAi phenotype observation and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: 924 transcript clusters were classified as enriched in somatic neoblasts.
claims.source: To elucidate genes enriched in somatic neoblasts, transcripts enriched in sorted proliferating cells of intact worms (Figure 3A), hatchlings (Figure 3E), and amputated heads (Figure 3F) were overlapped, resulting in 956 transcript clusters (Figure 3G). We further filtered this list by excluding germline enriched transcripts (Figure 3D), even though the overlap was minimal and 924 out of 956 transcript clusters remained and were classified as enriched in somatic neoblasts (Figure 3H and Figure 1—source data 2)
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from overlapping analyses and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The somatic neoblast list contains 26 S. mediterranea 'Neoblast' marker homologs out of the 157 annotated in the transcriptome, which is a 7.9-fold enrichment (p<10−15) relative to the random distribution.
claims.source: Indeed, this list contains 26 S. mediterranea 'Neoblast' marker homologs out of the 157 annotated in the transcriptome (Figure 1—source data 2), which is a 7.9-fold enrichment (p<10−15) relative to the random distribution (Figure 1—source data 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis with statistical test.

claims.claim: 357 transcript clusters enriched in somatic neoblasts were termed Stringent Neoblast candidate genes.
claims.source: To further narrow the list of genes enriched in somatic neoblasts, we overlapped transcript clusters identified as somatic neoblasts by the FACS approach (Figure 3H) with the irradiation-derived list of transcript clusters enriched in proliferating cells (Figure 2C). This resulted in 357 transcript clusters enriched in somatic neoblasts (Figure 3H), which we termed Stringent Neoblast candidate genes (Figure 1—source data 2 and Figure 3—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from overlapping analyses and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is highly enriched in the Stringent Neoblast list and contains 22 out of the 157 'Neoblast'-annotated transcripts (17.3-fold enrichment, p<10−15).
claims.source: The previously mentioned GO term enrichments characteristic of neoblast remained in this narrowed down list (Figure 1—source data 1), and, the Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is highly enriched and contains 22 out of the 157 'Neoblast'-annotated transcripts (17.3-fold enrichment, p<10−15, Figure 1—source data 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis with statistical test.

claims.claim: 211 out of the 357 Stringent Neoblast transcript clusters have identifiable human homologs representing 159 different human genes.
claims.source: Furthermore, 211 out of the 357 Stringent Neoblast transcript clusters have identifiable human homologs representing 159 different human genes (Figure 1—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as an annotation result.

claims.claim: Out of the 14 genes tested by RNAi, 5 gave the fast phenotype: Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a.
claims.source: During the screen, we focused on genes giving fast and robust phenotypes. In other words, phenotypes, which were observed within 3 weeks, in all treated worms, based on morphology. Out of the 14 genes tested, 5 gave the fast phenotype: Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a (Figure 4A and Figure 3—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from the RNAi screen and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The previously described phenotype for Mlig-piwi was confirmed.
claims.source: In addition, the previously described phenotype for Mlig-piwi (De Mulder et al., 2009) was confirmed, and two less severe phenotypes were found: Mlig-pcna and Mlig-cdc20 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a validation result with citation and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control intact animals, the number of mitotic cells in intact worms is significantly decreased during RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p=0.001, t-test), and Mlig-rpa3 (p=0.048, t-test).
claims.source: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control intact animals, the number of mitotic cells in intact worms is significantly decreased during RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p=0.001, t-test), and Mlig-rpa3 (p=0.048, t-test).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical tests.

claims.claim: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control cut worms, there are significantly less mitotic cells for RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rpa3 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-cdk1 (p<0.001, t-test), and Mlig-h2a (p=0.027).
claims.source: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control cut worms, there are significantly less mitotic cells for RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rpa3 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-cdk1 (p<0.001, t-test), and Mlig-h2a (p=0.027).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical tests.

claims.claim: In case of Mlig-ddx39, less than five mitotic cells per worm are observed in both intact and cut individuals.
claims.source: In case of Mlig-ddx39, less than five mitotic cells per worm are observed in both intact and cut individuals.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from mitotic labeling.

claims.claim: RNAi of Mlig-rrm1 results in a significant decrease of mitotic cells after tail amputation (p=0.008, t-test).
claims.source: RNAi of Mlig-rrm1 even results in a significant decrease of mitotic cells after tail amputation (p=0.008, t-test).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical test.

claims.claim: In the case of Mlig-h2a(RNAi) and Mlig-piwi(RNAi), amputation of the tail still results in a significantly increased amount of mitotic neoblasts (Mlig-h2a: p=0.001, t-test; Mlig-piwi: p<0.001, t-test).
claims.source: In the case of Mlig-h2a(RNAi) and Mlig-piwi(RNAi), amputation of the tail still results in a significantly increased amount of mitotic neoblasts (Mlig-h2a: p=0.001, t-test; Mlig-piwi: p<0.001, t-test).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical tests.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx39 gene proved to be the most severe phenotype of all screened candidates.
claims.source: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx39 gene proved to be the most severe phenotype of all screened candidates.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the RNAi screen.

claims.claim: In situ hybridization performed on adults and juveniles revealed the typical expression pattern of a gene enriched in proliferating cells for Mlig-ddx39.
claims.source: In situ hybridization performed on adults and juveniles revealed the typical expression pattern of a gene enriched in proliferating cells (Figure 5A), known from the published expression of piwi (De Mulder et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Both Mlig-ddx39 and Mlig-piwi1 are expressed in the testes, ovaries, developing eggs and the somatic neoblasts, visualized by bilateral bands.
claims.source: Both genes are expressed in the testes, ovaries, developing eggs and the somatic neoblasts, visualized by bilateral bands (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: In situ hybridization 12 hr post-amputation confirmed the expression of Mlig-ddx39 and Mlig-piwi1 in the blastema region.
claims.source: In situ hybridization 12 hr post-amputation confirmed the expression of Mlig-ddx39 and Mlig-piwi1 in the blastema region, which consists of proliferating neoblasts (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: A combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH / Macpiwi1 antibody labeling revealed cells co-expressing Mlig-ddx39 and Macpiwi1 in the testes, ovaries and somatic neoblasts.
claims.source: A combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH / Macpiwi1 antibody labeling revealed cells co-expressing Mlig-ddx39 and Macpiwi1 in the testes, ovaries and somatic neoblasts (Figure 5E–G).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from FISH and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: A combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH/phospho-histone H3 antibody mitotic labeling revealed expression of Mlig-ddx39 in the proliferating cells of blastema.
claims.source: Furthermore, a combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH/phospho-histone H3 antibody mitotic labeling revealed expression of Mlig-ddx39 in the proliferating cells of blastema (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from FISH and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Many of the M. lignano transcripts identified as enriched in proliferating cells by the irradiation approach have homologs within the set of X1 neoblast transcripts in Schmidtea.
claims.source: Many of the M. lignano transcripts identified as enriched in proliferating cells by the irradiation approach have homologs within the set of X1 neoblast transcripts in Schmidtea (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A,C), and the overlap is 3.78-fold higher than expected from random distribution (Figure 1—source data 4), suggesting the presence of the subset of genes with conserved neoblast function in flatworms.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The overlap between M. lignano neoblast genes and Schmidtea X1 genes is 3.78-fold higher than expected from random distribution.
claims.source: Many of the M. lignano transcripts identified as enriched in proliferating cells by the irradiation approach have homologs within the set of X1 neoblast transcripts in Schmidtea (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A,C), and the overlap is 3.78-fold higher than expected from random distribution (Figure 1—source data 4), suggesting the presence of the subset of genes with conserved neoblast function in flatworms.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis.

claims.claim: There is a substantial overlap between Macrostomum neoblast and irradiation categories and mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes.
claims.source: Furthermore, comparison with mammalian genes known to be involved in pluripotency (Tang et al., 2010) shows results similar to those previously reported for Schmidtea (Onal et al., 2012), with a substantial overlap between Macrostomum neoblast and irradiation categories and mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D), which are 4.08-fold overrepresented in the stringent neoblast category (Figure 1—source data 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis with citations and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes are 4.08-fold overrepresented in the stringent neoblast category.
claims.source: Furthermore, comparison with mammalian genes known to be involved in pluripotency (Tang et al., 2010) shows results similar to those previously reported for Schmidtea (Onal et al., 2012), with a substantial overlap between Macrostomum neoblast and irradiation categories and mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D), which are 4.08-fold overrepresented in the stringent neoblast category (Figure 1—source data 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis.

claims.claim: Pluripotency repressor genes are nearly completely excluded from the neoblast category.
claims.source: At the same time, pluripotency repressor genes are nearly completely excluded from the neoblast category (Figure 1—source data 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis.

claims.claim: The transcripts which are enriched in the proliferating germline cells of M. lignano only show a small overlap with known regulators of germ cell development in S. mediterranea and genes which are enriched in or specific for the sexual strain compared to the asexual strain of S. mediterranea.
claims.source: The transcripts which are enriched in the proliferating germline cells of M. lignano only show a small overlap with known regulators of germ cell development in S. mediterranea and genes which are enriched in or specific for the sexual strain compared to the asexual strain of S. mediterranea (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The planarian germline set is based primarily on the differentiated cells, while the Macrostomum set is enriched for genes expressed in proliferating germline cells, which explains the minimal overlap between these sets.
claims.source: The planarian germline set is based primarily on the differentiated cells, while the Macrostomum set is enriched for genes expressed in proliferating germline cells, which explains the minimal overlap between these sets.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed difference.

claims.claim: Both irradiation and FACS techniques proved to be efficient in determining the gene expression profile of planarian neoblasts.
claims.source: Both techniques proved to be efficient in determining the gene expression profile of planarian neoblasts (Reddien and Sánchez Alvarado, 2004; Hayashi et al., 2006; Rossi et al., 2007; Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Blythe et al., 2010; Galloni, 2012; Shibata et al., 2012; Solana et al., 2012) and were, therefore, our first choice.
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies using these methods.

claims.claim: The results of the three doses of 70 Gy within 1 day method on the level of morphology, mortality, and decreasing number of proliferating cells are very similar to the previously described fractionated protocol performing several doses distributed over 9 days and accumulating in 210 Gy.
claims.source: This differs from the published lethal fractionated protocol performing several doses distributed over 9 days and accumulating in 210 Gy (De Mulder et al., 2010). However, the results of both methods on the level of morphology, mortality, and decreasing number of proliferating cells are very similar.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a comparison to a previous method with citation.

claims.claim: The effect of irradiation on gene expression is fast and mainly takes place within the first 12 hr after the last irradiation pulse.
claims.source: The effect of irradiation on gene expression is fast and mainly takes place within the first 12 hr after the last irradiation pulse (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from temporal gene expression analysis and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Irradiation causes a broad stress reaction to the cells, triggered by global DNA damage, but also includes changes due to neoblast elimination.
claims.source: It was shown before that irradiation causes a broad stress reaction to the cells, triggered by global DNA damage, but also includes changes due to neoblast elimination (Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Solana et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Hoechst labeling has been commonly used to isolate proliferating cells in planarians.
claims.source: Hoechst labeling has been commonly used to isolate proliferating cells in planarians (Hayashi et al., 2006; Higuchi et al., 2007; Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Shibata et al., 2012), and the 4C DNA content is one of the main characteristics of the X1 cells, which are highly enriched in neoblasts (Hayashi et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: The 4C DNA content is one of the main characteristics of the X1 cells, which are highly enriched in neoblasts.
claims.source: Hoechst labeling has been commonly used to isolate proliferating cells in planarians (Hayashi et al., 2006; Higuchi et al., 2007; Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Shibata et al., 2012), and the 4C DNA content is one of the main characteristics of the X1 cells, which are highly enriched in neoblasts (Hayashi et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: 6.5% of all cells in M. lignano are neoblasts.
claims.source: This population is much smaller than the 2C population, as 'only' 6.5% of all cells in M. lignano are neoblasts (Bode et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: The FACS strategy has limitations, which is mainly the focus on actively dividing cells.
claims.source: As all approaches, the FACS strategy has its own limitations, which is mainly the focus on actively dividing cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method.

claims.claim: Genes specific for the small population of quiescent neoblasts will be missed by the FACS approach.
claims.source: Consequently, genes specific for the small population of quiescent neoblasts (Verdoodt et al., 2012) will be missed.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the FACS limitation with citation.

claims.claim: About half of the identified transcript clusters are specific for the used method (irradiation or FACS).
claims.source: The bias is further shown by the fact that about half of the identified transcript clusters are specific for the used method.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from comparing the two methods.

claims.claim: 3374 transcript clusters are identified with both irradiation and FACS approaches and represent a trustworthy selection of genes enriched in proliferating cells.
claims.source: The other half (3374 transcript clusters) are identified with both approaches and represent a trustworthy selection of genes enriched in proliferating cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from comparing the two methods.

claims.claim: Much more transcript clusters are enriched in the germline (2739) than in the somatic neoblasts (956).
claims.source: Interestingly, much more transcript clusters are enriched in the germline (2739) than in the somatic neoblasts (956).
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from the analysis.

claims.claim: The majority of genes enriched in the germline seem to be specific for the testes.
claims.source: In situ hybridization experiments show that the majority of genes enriched in the germline seem to be specific for the testes (Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH experiments.

claims.claim: The large amount of testes-specific genes reflects the functional complexity of the testes and the requirement of producing highly elaborate sperm.
claims.source: It has been suggested that the large amount of testes-specific genes reflects the functional complexity of the testes and the requirement of producing highly elaborate sperm (Arbore et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a suggested explanation with citation.

claims.claim: The small overlap between M. lignano germline genes and planarian germline genes can be explained by the difference between proliferating and differentiated germline cells.
claims.source: When considering genes regulating the development, regeneration, and maintenance of gonads and gametes, it is important to distinguish between the proliferating and differentiated germline cells. This can explain the small overlap between the transcripts enriched in the proliferating germline cells of M. lignano and the published datasets of Schmidtea germline genes, which primarily include transcripts specific for differentiated germline cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed difference.

claims.claim: Despite the enrichment in somatic neoblasts, genes enriched in somatic neoblasts are also expressed in the gonads.
claims.source: In situ hybridization (ISH) of transcripts enriched in somatic neoblasts showed that, despite the enrichment, these genes are also expressed in the gonads.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from ISH experiments.

claims.claim: Due to limitations of the ISH technique to visualize single neoblasts scattered in the mesenchyme, expression in the gonads is more obvious than expression in the somatic neoblasts.
claims.source: Due to limitations of the ISH technique to visualize single neoblasts scattered in the mesenchyme, expression in the gonads is more obvious than expression in the somatic neoblasts (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a technical limitation.

claims.claim: It is important to develop more sensitive methods for visualizing gene expression in single cells in M. lignano.
claims.source: Therefore, it is important to develop more sensitive methods for visualizing gene expression in single cells in M. lignano, as this will be essential to confirm the specificity of genes for the somatic neoblasts or the germline.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a need for future work.

claims.claim: It is unclear whether genes specifically expressed in somatic neoblasts of M. lignano do not exist or cannot be identified yet due to technical limitations.
claims.source: The current lack of genes specifically expressed in somatic neoblasts of M. lignano is fascinating, and it is unclear whether they do not exist and neoblasts residing in mesenchyme and in gonads are largely similar, or cannot be identified yet due to technical limitations.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an open question.

claims.claim: Homologues of ribonucleotide reductase M1 (RRM1), replication protein A3 (RPA3), cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1), proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), and cell division cycle protein 20 (CDC20) are encoding proteins previously linked to cell cycle processes.
claims.source: Homologues of ribonucleotide reductase M1 (RRM1), replication protein A3 (RPA3), cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1), proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), and cell division cycle protein 20 (CDC20) are encoding proteins previously linked to cell cycle processes (Lee and Nurse, 1987; Travali et al., 1989; Henricksen et al., 1994; Parker et al., 1995; Weinstein, 1997).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies on these proteins.

claims.claim: Histone family member A (H2A) was shown to be important for packaging DNA into chromatin and is consequently involved in gene expression regulation.
claims.source: Histone family member A (H2A) was shown to be important for packaging DNA into chromatin and is consequently involved in gene expression regulation (Mariño-Ramírez et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: DEAD box polypeptide 39 (DDX39) was not previously studied in the context of in vivo stem cell functionality.
claims.source: To our knowledge, DEAD box polypeptide 39 (DDX39) was not previously studied in the context of in vivo stem cell functionality.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a novel finding.

claims.claim: All five robust RNAi phenotypes suggest problems with cell turnover during both homeostasis and regeneration.
claims.source: All five robust phenotypes suggest problems with cell turnover during both homeostasis and regeneration.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the RNAi phenotypes.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx39 resulted in the death of all worms within 3 weeks.
claims.source: In case of the DDX39 homologue, all treated worms died within 3 weeks.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from the RNAi experiment.

claims.claim: The regeneration phenotype of Mlig-piwi is less severe than that of the other five genes, as a small blastema can be observed in several worms.
claims.source: The regeneration phenotype is, however, less severe than that of the other five genes, as a small blastema can be observed in several worms.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from the RNAi experiment.

claims.claim: The Mlig-cdc20(RNAi) phenotype is limited within the first 3 weeks of treatment as the only effect is the disintegration of gonads, and defects in regeneration are not observed.
claims.source: The Mlig-cdc20(RNAi) phenotype is limited within the first 3 weeks of treatment as the only effect is the disintegration of gonads, and defects in regeneration are not observed (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from the RNAi experiment and shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Mitotic labeling revealed that already during the 10th day of Mlig-ddx39 treatment almost no mitotic cells can be observed in both cut and intact animals.
claims.source: The mitotic labeling revealed that already during the 10th day of treatment almost no mitotic cells can be observed in both cut and intact Mlig-ddx39(RNAi) animals, suggesting the fast elimination of proliferating cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from mitotic labeling.

claims.claim: Mlig-ddx39 is proposed as a positive control for RNAi experiments in M. lignano.
claims.source: Based on these results, we propose the use of Mlig-ddx39 as a positive control for RNAi experiments in M. lignano, which is already a common practice in our laboratory.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the RNAi results.

claims.claim: Mlig-ddx39 could be a convenient marker for proliferating cells.
claims.source: In addition, the ISH results showing enriched expression in the gonads and in somatic neoblasts in both the intact body and in the blastema indicate that Mlig-ddx39 could be a convenient marker for proliferating cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the ISH results.

claims.claim: ddx39 is highly conserved in different species, as all members of the DEAD box RNA helicase family.
claims.source: Interestingly, ddx39 is highly conserved in different species, as all members of the DEAD box RNA helicase family.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of the gene family.

claims.claim: DEAD box RNA helicase family genes include a common D-E-A-D (Asp-Glu-Ala-Asp) motive and are known for their roles in RNA metabolism.
claims.source: These genes include a common D-E-A-D (Asp-Glu-Ala-Asp) motive and are known for their roles in RNA metabolism (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Functions of ddx39 have been linked to mRNA export, which was demonstrated in D. melanogaster and C. elegans.
claims.source: Functions of ddx39 have been linked to mRNA export, which was demonstrated in D. melanogaster (Eberl et al., 1997) and C. elegans (MacMorris et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: ddx39 was shown to be important for regeneration and development of limbs in X. laevis.
claims.source: Moreover, ddx39 was shown to be important for regeneration and development of limbs in X. laevis (Wilson et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: An online interface to the generated datasets is available at http://neoblast.macgenome.org.

claims.claim: The de novo M. lignano transcriptome and generated sets of genes enriched in the germline and somatic neoblasts are valuable resources for further development of this species as a model organism for stem cell research.

results.result: A high-quality de novo transcriptome assembly (MLRNA150904) was generated for M. lignano using over one billion sequencing reads from 22 libraries. The assembly contains 60,180 transcripts explaining >90% of reads, with a TransRate score of 0.4367 ranking it in the top 5% of published assemblies, and includes 247/248 core eukaryotic genes and 296/303 complete BUSCO genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C32-C48 collectively demonstrate a comprehensive and high-quality transcriptome assembly. The use of multiple library types (C33), assembly strategies (C34), and rigorous quality metrics (C36-C42) including comparison to established benchmarks provides strong evidence. The completeness metrics (C40-C41) and comparative quality assessments (C37-C38) support the claim of a high-quality resource.

results.result: Irradiation with three doses of 70 Gy within one day effectively eliminates proliferating cells including neoblasts within 12 hours, as evidenced by loss of mitotic activity, morphological changes, eventual 100% mortality by day 35, and specific downregulation of 8,929 transcript clusters enriched for neoblast markers and cell cycle processes.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C58 provide converging evidence from morphology (C50-C51), mitotic labeling (C52-C53), and transcriptional profiling (C54-C57) that the irradiation protocol specifically and rapidly eliminates proliferating cells. The 3.3-fold enrichment of S. mediterranea neoblast markers (C56) with statistical significance (p<10^-15) and GO term analysis (C55) strongly support the specificity of the effect.

results.result: A FACS-based approach using Hoechst staining successfully isolated proliferating cells (4C DNA content) from differentiated cells (2C), identifying 7,124 transcript clusters enriched in proliferating cells with 2.68-fold enrichment for S. mediterranea neoblast markers (p<10^-15).
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C63 demonstrate a validated FACS strategy. The six-fold reduction in 4C cells upon irradiation (C60) validates gate specificity, while the enrichment of neoblast markers (C63) and appropriate GO terms (C62) confirms biological relevance. The convergence with irradiation data strengthens confidence in the approach.

results.result: By comparing proliferating cells from intact worms, hatchlings, and amputated heads (which lack gonads), 2,739 transcript clusters enriched in germline were identified and validated by ISH (27/27 genes) and functional RNAi showing gonad-specific phenotypes for Mlig-cpeb1 and Mlig-ddx6.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C69 describe a logical experimental design exploiting developmental stages lacking gonads to identify germline genes. The 100% validation rate by ISH (C66) and functional confirmation by RNAi (C67-C69) provide strong orthogonal support for the germline gene set.

results.result: By overlapping FACS-derived proliferating cells from intact worms, hatchlings, and amputated heads, then filtering germline genes, 924 transcript clusters were classified as somatic neoblast-enriched. Further intersection with irradiation data yielded 357 'Stringent Neoblast' genes showing 17.3-fold enrichment for S. mediterranea neoblast markers (p<10^-15).
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C74 describe a rigorous filtering strategy combining multiple experimental approaches. The progressive enrichment from 7.9-fold (C71) to 17.3-fold (C73) for neoblast markers demonstrates successful refinement. The statistical significance and identification of human homologs (C74) support the quality of this gene set.

results.result: RNAi screening of 14 Stringent Neoblast genes identified five (Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, Mlig-h2a) with fast, robust phenotypes affecting homeostasis and regeneration, confirmed by significant reductions in mitotic cells during both homeostasis and regeneration (p<0.05).
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C81 and C8-C12 provide functional validation of the transcriptomic predictions. The morphological phenotypes, quantified mitotic labeling with statistical tests (C77-C81), and effects on both homeostasis and regeneration provide strong evidence for essential roles in neoblast function. The confirmation of the known Mlig-piwi phenotype (C76) serves as a positive control.

results.result: Mlig-ddx39 showed the most severe RNAi phenotype with 100% lethality within 3 weeks and near-complete loss of mitotic cells by day 10. ISH and FISH confirmed expression in proliferating cells (testes, ovaries, somatic neoblasts, blastema), supporting its utility as a neoblast marker and positive RNAi control.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C87, C118, C121-C123 provide comprehensive characterization of Mlig-ddx39. The severe phenotype (C82, C118), rapid loss of mitotic cells (C121), and expression pattern matching known neoblast markers like piwi (C83-C87) strongly support its proposed utility. However, claims C122-C123 are proposals for future use rather than demonstrated applications.

results.result: Comparative analysis revealed evolutionary conservation of neoblast genes, with M. lignano proliferating cell genes showing 3.78-fold enrichment for S. mediterranea X1 neoblast genes and 4.08-fold enrichment for mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes, while pluripotency repressor genes were nearly excluded.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C92 demonstrate evolutionary conservation through comparative genomics. The significant enrichments (C89, C91) and specific exclusion of repressor genes (C92) suggest conserved molecular mechanisms. However, the analysis relies on homology assignments which may have limitations, and the functional significance of these overlaps requires experimental validation.

results.result: M. lignano germline genes show minimal overlap with S. mediterranea germline genes, explained by M. lignano genes representing proliferating germline cells while planarian datasets primarily represent differentiated germline cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C94, C109 provide a logical explanation for the observed lack of overlap. The distinction between proliferating and differentiated germline cells is biologically sound and consistent with the experimental design. However, this remains an interpretation rather than a directly tested hypothesis.

results.result: Approximately half of the identified transcript clusters are method-specific (irradiation or FACS), while 3,374 transcript clusters identified by both approaches represent a trustworthy selection of genes enriched in proliferating cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 acknowledge methodological biases while identifying a high-confidence gene set. The overlap of 3,374 genes between methods provides internal validation, though the claim that this represents a 'trustworthy' selection is somewhat subjective without additional validation.

results.result: More transcript clusters are enriched in germline (2,739) than somatic neoblasts (956), with the majority being testes-specific, potentially reflecting the functional complexity of testes and elaborate sperm production.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C107 are supported by the data and ISH validation. However, claim C108 is a speculative explanation cited from previous work rather than a finding of this study. The interpretation is plausible but not directly tested.

results.result: Genes classified as somatic neoblast-enriched are also expressed in gonads, with gonad expression more obvious than somatic neoblast expression due to ISH technical limitations. It remains unclear whether truly somatic neoblast-specific genes exist or cannot yet be identified.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C113 acknowledge important technical limitations and interpretive uncertainty. The observation (C110) is supported by ISH data, and the technical limitation (C111) is reasonable. However, claims C112-C113 are speculative about future needs and unresolved questions rather than supported findings.

results.result: The five genes with robust RNAi phenotypes include known cell cycle regulators (RRM1, RPA3, CDK1, PCNA, CDC20) and histone H2A, while DDX39 had not been previously studied in the context of in vivo stem cell functionality. All phenotypes suggest problems with cell turnover during homeostasis and regeneration.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C117 provide appropriate context for the RNAi results. The characterization of known genes (C114-C115) is well-supported by citations, the novelty of DDX39 (C116) is appropriately stated, and the interpretation of phenotypes (C117) is consistent with the observed data.

results.result: The Mlig-piwi RNAi phenotype is less severe than the five robust phenotypes, showing small blastema formation, while Mlig-cdc20 RNAi shows only gonad disintegration without regeneration defects within 3 weeks.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C120 describe phenotypic observations that are supported by the presented data and figures. These represent valid but less dramatic findings compared to the five robust phenotypes.

results.result: DDX39 is highly conserved across species as a member of the DEAD box RNA helicase family, with known functions in mRNA export (D. melanogaster, C. elegans) and importance for limb regeneration and development in X. laevis.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-C127 provide appropriate background on DDX39 from the literature. These are well-supported by citations and provide context for the M. lignano findings, though they represent prior knowledge rather than new results.

results.result: Both irradiation and FACS techniques have been proven efficient for determining neoblast gene expression profiles in planarians. The modified irradiation protocol (3×70 Gy in 1 day) produces similar results to the published fractionated protocol (210 Gy over 9 days), with gene expression changes occurring rapidly within 12 hours.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C98 provide methodological validation and comparison. The efficiency of both methods is supported by citations (C95), the protocol comparison is data-supported (C96), and the temporal dynamics are demonstrated (C97). Claim C98 appropriately cites previous work on irradiation effects.

results.result: The FACS strategy based on Hoechst labeling and 4C DNA content has been commonly used in planarians and successfully adapted for M. lignano, though it has limitations including focus on actively dividing cells and inability to capture quiescent neoblasts (6.5% of all cells).
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C103 provide methodological context and acknowledge limitations. The use of Hoechst labeling is well-supported by citations (C99-C100), the proportion of neoblasts is cited (C101), and the limitations are appropriately acknowledged (C102-C103).

results.result: An online interface (http://neoblast.macgenome.org) was developed to provide access to the datasets. The transcriptome and gene sets are proposed as valuable resources for stem cell research, with the RNAi screen identifying novel genes essential for neoblast functionality, and ddx39 suggested as a positive control and marker.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C131 describe resources and conclusions. The online interface (C128) is a concrete deliverable. Claims C129-C131 are appropriate summary statements, though they include speculative elements about future value and utility rather than demonstrated applications.

results.result: Background claims establish M. lignano as a regeneration-capable basal flatworm with neoblasts, complementing planarian models, with limited existing molecular markers (piwi, vasa) motivating the need for comprehensive transcriptomic characterization.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C31 provide essential background and motivation. Most are supported by appropriate citations to previous work (C13-C30) or represent established knowledge about the organism (C1, C7, C20-C26). The motivation (C4, C31) logically follows from the limited existing markers (C30).
